what_this_is_not: R values are copied from the tracked fixture. Julia values are computed fresh by tools/true_parity_julia_receipts.jl, which repeats the computation of the cited twin test with the same inputs and settings; R was not run and is not recomputed here.

cases.quantity: maximised weighted objective of the Poisson fit (the logLik for the unweighted fit)
cases.note: R: wide_df route, traits() route, one weight per unit, response = 'include'. R traits() route: gllvmTMB(traits(t1, ..., t6) ~ 1 + latent(1 | unit, d = 1, unique = FALSE), family = poisson(), weights = <length-n vector>), the public route. Julia: fit_gllvm(Y; family = Poisson(), K = 1, ...), Y with a placeholder 0 at the 14 cells and mask = the observed cells; weights = w_unit. p = 6, n = 120 (sha256 checked), one Poisson data set, one latent factor; every R fit converged with a positive-definite Hessian. A weight multiplies its cell's conditional log-density on both sides (gllvmTMB weights_i in src/gllvmTMB.cpp; GLLVModels src/families/laplace.jl). gllvmTMB's logLik() aborts for non-unit weights, so the compared number is the maximised weighted objective (R -fit$opt$objective, Julia fit.loglik; logLik() for the unweighted fit). The twin test also asserts that every weighted R objective differs from the unweighted one by more than 1, so the weights are applied, not ignored. The sign of a one-axis loading is not identified, so loadings are compared through Lambda Lambda'.
